text:
alex_sales: Kicking off the 'heartbeat' POC for Prospect Nimbus — objective is to validate sustained throughput and p99 tail latency for short chat-like prompts. Target: 1k sustained qps with p99 < 200ms for 0.5-1.5s generation windows. Wed 9–11 PST. Need ops + SRE + SE + pricing.

maya_se: Plan looks good. A few clarifying Qs:
- Are we running a homogeneous request size (avg 25–40 tokens) or a mixed workload with a small percentage of long contexts?
- Which model & quantization profile do we pin for the test?

zach_sre: Suggest fixed short prompts for baseline then 10% long tails to simulate real traffic. Load config I'm going to run locally: `wrk -t12 -c1200 -d30m --latency http://redwood-poc.internal/api/v1/generate -s scripts/nimbus_short.lua` — script sends JSON with 30 token prompt at ~1k rps.

maya_se: For model pin, let's use `prod-7b-8k-quant` with batch_size=8, auto-prefix-cache enabled. Add KV cache warmup step (100k tokens) before the steady window. That drops per-token time.

ops_bot: deploy: canary rollout to dedicated-poc-cluster starting 08:30 PST — monitoring hooks: /alerts/throughput, /dash/p99, /dash/cpu-gpu-util.

alex_sales: Customer pricing question: at 1k sustained qps what's the ballpark incremental cost (hourly) for Dedicated? They asked whether there's a per-hour burn vs. per-token delta.

emma_research: Quick back-of-envelope: with quantized runtime estimate ~0.5 tokens/ms GPU-side, at 30 tokens/request => 15ms GPU; accounting infra and batching overhead call it 35ms/request -> ~28.5k reqs/sec per GPU? That math seems off, recheck.

maya_se: Let's be conservative: measured on prod-7b-8k-quant in previous POC: ~0.9ms/token end-to-end at 8-bit with batching tuned -> ~27ms per 30-token request. At 1k qps that's 27k tokens/s. If token billing is applied, map to $/token + reserved GPU cost. I'll post a quick estimate after lunch.

zach_sre: Enterprise/security blocker: Nimbus requires HSM-backed keys and audit log proof. For Dedicated we can integrate external KMS (customer-managed) but need SSO + IP allowlist configured. That will add ~3 business days to provisioning.

alex_sales: Noted — I'll surface that to their security contact. Any quick mitigations to keep the POC moving while getting KMS set up?

maya_se: We can run an isolated POC with redwood-managed keys but with strict ephemeral logs and signed attestations for the test window. Make clear this is temporary and not acceptable for production.

emma_research: Results writeup plan: baseline (short prompts), tail test (10% long), degradation test (gradually reduce batch_size to simulate small clients), and failover test (simulate region fallback). Each run: 30 minutes steady-state, collect p50/p95/p99, GPU util, request queue lengths, and token burn.

zach_sre: Load generator snippet for reproducibility:
```
wrk -t12 -c1200 -d1800s --latency http://redwood-poc.internal/api/v1/generate \
  -s scripts/nimbus_short.lua --timeout 60000
```
Lua payload sample: `return [[{"prompt":"<short chat msg>","max_tokens":40}]]`

alex_sales: Good. Emma — any quick numbers you can drop for pricing slide to show the customer during the kickoff? They want a 1-line number: "approx cost per 1k qps (hour)"

emma_research: Put a conservative estimate in the deck: $6k/hr for reserved-capacity baseline at 1k qps on Dedicated (includes amortized GPU + infra + support). Add note: per-token billing on hosted would vary with prompt length; we'll follow up with a precise breakdown post-run.

maya_se: Ops checklist for Wed:
- Prewarm KV cache for 30m (maya)
- Provision temporary redwood-managed KMS for POC (zach)
- Load script + bench machines provisioned (ops_bot/ops)
- Pricing slide + SOW stub ready (alex)
- Monitoring dashboard link shared to Nimbus sec (zach)

ops_bot: ack: created runbook ticket #RB-4217 and dashboard `/dash/poc/nimbus-heartbeat`.

alex_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll confirm times with Nimbus and send calendar invites. Post the short-run results + 1-page summary in this thread. :thumbsup:
